name: enemies-r5
note: BL-17, owner 2026-11-12 (fourth round), one candidate each. Ogre: the r4 design kept but redrawn in the game's style (r4 was too realistic, the owner's reference photographs pulled it there; they are NOT refs here) and narrower. Ghost: no mouth, only the eyes floating in the dark hood. Phoenix: new, 2 x 2, hovering with its wings open.

ogre.prompt: RENDERING REFERENCE: the attached COW on magenta is one of this game's animals: match its rendering (soft painterly, flat colour with gentle shading, soft thick outlines, no texture, no background). STYLE REFERENCE, the most important image: the attached farm man on magenta is an APPROVED character of this game. The new creature must look drawn by the same hand on the same day, for the same storybook: the same chunky doll proportion (a big head, large expressive eyes, a short thick body, small feet), the same soft rendering; never realistic, never anatomical, never gory. THIS IS AN ENEMY the player fights: menacing in a storybook way (a scowl, bared teeth, a glare), but still charming and readable, something a child would call a monster and not be frightened by; no blood, no wounds. VIEW, the rule for every enemy (unlike this game's farm animals, which are drawn side-on): FRONT-FACING, like the player characters: upright and facing the viewer, the body square-ish to the viewer with a FAINT three-quarter turn, the head and the eyes turned a little toward the viewer's RIGHT, standing on ONE flat ground line, left and right sides roughly symmetrical, nothing trailing far outside the body's silhouette. SIBLINGS: the attached ZOMBIE and the attached red DEMON are approved enemies of this game: the ogre must look like the third of that set, painted the same way: the same simple rounded shapes, the same clean flat-ish colour with gentle soft shading, the same soft thick outlines, the same slightly big head and clear readable face. DESIGN REFERENCE: the attached OGRE is the first drawing of this enemy. Its DESIGN is right and is kept: the bald head with a rough strip of dark hair behind, the pointed ears, the heavy brow, the underbite with two short blunt tusks, the sallow olive skin (only slightly green), the bare chest and big belly, the dark leather wrappings on both forearms, the ragged dark brown kilt under a wide belt with an iron ring buckle, the wrapped shins, the huge bare feet, both arms hanging at its sides with EMPTY hands. But it was painted TOO REALISTICALLY for this game, and too wide. REDRAW it in the game's storybook style: NO skin texture, no pores, no mottling, no blotches, no wrinkles, no realistic muscle anatomy, no photographic lighting: smooth simple forms in flat colour with a soft shadow side, like the zombie's skin and the demon's skin. A somewhat bigger head than the first drawing (about a quarter of its height) with bigger, clearer eyes and a simpler face; still grim and scowling, not goofy. SUBJECT: the OGRE as described, and NARROWER: the shoulders less broad, the arms hanging closer to the body, the legs closer together: the whole figure about two thirds as wide as it is tall. It holds NOTHING. Keep it at the game's scale: it is seen about 60 pixels wide on the board, so big plain shapes, a strong silhouette, flat areas of colour, no fine detail, no small accessories. COLOUR: never pink, never magenta, never purple anywhere on it. The LAST attached image is a layout guide: a pure magenta (#FF00FF) field with a thin grid, a 1 x 1 box outlined in the middle (one board tile) and a dashed half-height box directly above it (the headroom); the reference character stands in that box with its head in the headroom. ONE FIGURE ONLY, nothing else in the picture: no building, no props on the ground, no scene. Draw it standing on the box's bottom edge and bigger than the reference character: about one and a half times as tall, and about one and a half times as broad, its feet on the box's bottom edge, its head near the top of the headroom. A soft contact shadow directly under it; leave every other pixel pure solid magenta: no grass, no ground, no frame, no text.

phoenix.prompt: RENDERING REFERENCE: the attached COW on magenta is one of this game's animals: match its rendering (soft painterly, flat colour with gentle shading, soft thick outlines, no texture, no background). STYLE REFERENCE, the most important image: the attached farm man on magenta is an APPROVED character of this game. The new creature must look drawn by the same hand on the same day, for the same storybook: the same chunky doll proportion (a big head, large expressive eyes, a short thick body, small feet), the same soft rendering; never realistic, never anatomical, never gory. THIS IS AN ENEMY the player fights: menacing in a storybook way (a scowl, bared teeth, a glare), but still charming and readable, something a child would call a monster and not be frightened by; no blood, no wounds. VIEW, the rule for every enemy (unlike this game's farm animals, which are drawn side-on): FRONT-FACING, like the player characters: upright and facing the viewer, the body square-ish to the viewer with a FAINT three-quarter turn, the head and the eyes turned a little toward the viewer's RIGHT, left and right sides roughly symmetrical. SIBLING: the attached red DEMON is an approved enemy of this game that also hovers with its wings open: the phoenix must look painted by the same hand, in the same simple shapes, clean flat-ish colour and soft thick outlines. SUBJECT: a PHOENIX, a great bird of fire, the strongest creature in the game, hovering upright and FACING THE VIEWER with both wings spread wide open to the sides, like the demon. BODY: a proud eagle-like bird with a deep chest; plumage of rich scarlet red on the body shading to bright orange and golden yellow at the tips of the wing feathers and the tail; a crest of three or four long flame-shaped golden feathers on the head; a hooked golden beak; fierce glowing amber eyes under angry brows. WINGS: two big wings spread OPEN and slightly raised, each made of large simple flame-shaped feathers, red at the shoulder, then orange, then yellow at the tips. TAIL: a fan of four or five long flame-shaped tail feathers hanging down below the body, orange and gold. LEGS: two short golden legs with dark talons tucked under the body, holding NOTHING. FIRE: the feather tips are drawn AS flames, as solid painted shapes that are part of the bird; no loose sparks, no smoke, no separate fire around it, no glow or light spilling onto the background; every part is OPAQUE. It HOVERS: the tips of the tail feathers hang clearly above the ground with empty space under them. Keep it at the game's scale: it is seen about 90 pixels wide on the board, so big plain shapes, a strong silhouette, flat areas of colour, no fine detail, no small accessories. COLOUR: reds, oranges and golds, bright and saturated; never pink, never magenta, never purple anywhere on it. The LAST attached image is a layout guide: a pure magenta (#FF00FF) field with a thin grid, a 1 x 1 box outlined in the middle (one board tile) and a dashed half-height box directly above it (the headroom); the reference character stands in that box with its head in the headroom. ONE FIGURE ONLY, nothing else in the picture: no building, no props on the ground, no scene. Draw it hovering over the box, bigger than the reference character: about one and a half times as tall from the crest to the tail tips, the tail tips a little above the box's bottom edge, the crest near the top of the headroom; the open wings spread well past the box's sides, about as wide across as the bird is tall. A soft oval shadow on the ground directly below it, at the box's bottom edge, not touching the tail; leave every other pixel pure solid magenta: no grass, no ground, no frame, no text.
